question: The source text states its own address algorithm for the eighty-one heads. Does it agree with the coordinate formula used in the earlier notes of this line? Which divisions of the eighty-one heads are definable in the address algebra, and is the split at forty-seven a congruence? Since two heads that the text pairs lie across that split, is the split a translate of a boundary that the text does pair? Is the river diagram's pairing a quotient, and is the reported calendar near miss closer than the grid of head boundaries already forces?
level: External exact integer arithmetic, exact rational arithmetic and exhaustive checks over declared finite sets; no corpus file is opened, no corpus count is imported or recomputed, and every acceptance test compares integers or exact rationals
domain: The four-place ternary address space of eighty-one heads; the four clauses the source is quoted to state for the head number, transcribed here as declared increment tables; the nine heads with the last two places at their first value; the split of the head indices at forty-seven against every modulus from two to eighty-one; one displacement of the address space and its three-cycles; the river diagram's pairing of one to nine; and the calendar that the source text's own praise count defines
sources: The clauses this experiment cites are quoted verbatim in docs/research/0217-*.md from the project author's own external record, https://github.com/mountain/wenyan-relation-learning at commit cfb6e4dc18425312447b01efd75b646d2ab1473e, which reports them from the transcribed classical text at data/corpus/works/太玄經.json. That file records its source site as zh.wikisource.org and its own licence note: the underlying classical works are public domain by age, and what is taken from Wikisource is its transcription, namely the choice of recension, the modern punctuation, the paragraphing and the character forms, with attribution recorded per section.

Nothing from that record is opened, read, executed or recomputed by this experiment. The four increment tables below are a transcription of four clauses the note quotes, declared here so that the map they generate can be computed and compared with the coordinate formula; the comparison is a check of the transcription's arithmetic and is not a collation against any edition.

text_address_increments.comment: The increment each place contributes at each of its three values, transcribed from the four clauses the note quotes verbatim: 家一置一，二置二，三置三 gives one, two, three for the family place; 部一勿增，二增三，三增六 gives zero, three, six for the section place; and likewise nine, eighteen and twenty-seven, fifty-four for the district and quarter places. The checker builds the head number from these four tables, so a transcription error fails the check.

quantifiers: All eighty-one heads for the two address formulas, the nine-row set and the three-cycle decomposition
All eighty moduli from two to eighty-one for the congruence question
All eighty-one heads for the order and orbit of the declared displacement
All nine numbers of the river diagram for the quotient
All twenty-four calendar nodes for the gap against the grid of head boundaries
grammar: exact integer arithmetic on the ternary places, with the head number recovered from the coordinates
exhaustive testing of membership in unions of residue classes, with a witness pair recorded for every failing modulus
exact rational arithmetic over Fraction for the calendar, with no floating-point value in any acceptance test
exact set comparisons on declared finite structures
acceptance: The four clauses transcribed into this contract from the source text's own statement of the head number generate all eighty-one heads, their place weights are the successive powers of three, and the map they generate is the coordinate formula used in the earlier notes

The nine heads whose last two places are at their first value are the declared nine, equally spaced by nine, exactly the fiber over two fixed places, and are defined by exactly two place constraints while the first two places run freely

The split at forty-seven is a union of residue classes modulo eighty-one only, which is trivial, and for every one of the other seventy-nine moduli there is a witness pair that breaks it; the two cases of the argument hold on the data
The same displacement carries the first pair of heads and the second pair of heads, so the boundary at forty-seven and forty-eight is the translate of the boundary at seven and eight
The displacement has order three, its orbits on the two pairs are seven forty-seven sixty-nine and eight forty-eight sixty-seven, and it splits all eighty-one heads into twenty-seven three-cycles
The river diagram's pairs are exactly the fibers of reduction modulo five on the numbers one to nine, every pair differing by five, and the label is a function of the residue class
The shift by five has no fixed point on the ten residues but exactly one when restricted to one to nine, namely five, which is why that pair is written with a number against itself

The source text's own numbers give thirty-six bundles of seven hundred twenty-nine praises, twenty-six thousand two hundred forty-four in all, which divided by seventy-two is three hundred sixty-four and a half days, so one praise is half a day and one head is nine praises
The split at forty-seven divides the seven hundred twenty-nine praises into four hundred twenty-three and three hundred six, that is two hundred eleven and a half and one hundred fifty-three days

Each calendar node's gap is its exact distance to the nearest of the eighty-one head boundaries, and those boundaries are a grid of spacing four and a half days, so every one of the twenty-four nodes is within nine quarters of a day of a boundary by construction and no data can change that

The reported node's gap to its nearest head boundary is forty-one twenty-fourths of a day, which is worse than the median node and ranks fourteenth of twenty-three by closeness, while another node is more than seventy-six times closer
protected: No corpus file is opened and no corpus count from any external repository is imported or recomputed here, and no measurement of any external record is reproduced. Four clauses of a classical text are quoted verbatim in the input document and transcribed here as declared increment tables; no edition is collated, no transcription is verified against one, and nothing from the named record is opened, read or executed
The formulas, the constants and the reported numbers are declared in this contract; the checker verifies their arithmetic and the structural consequences, and measures nothing
No claim about what any chapter, head or position means, and no claim about which transmitted reading is original

The address formula is checked against the four clauses the source is reported to state, not against a collated edition; this note does not perform that collation and does not claim it, and the check is of the transcription's arithmetic and not of the text

No claim that the split at forty-seven has no cause: the two negatives shown here are about definability in two declared algebras, and the external record's own remaining candidate, a transmitted editorial boundary, is neither tested nor excluded
No claim that the translate relation explains anything about the split; it is a structural coincidence in the text's own pairing and is recorded as such
No claim that the river diagram is or is not a historical source of anything; only that its pairing is a quotient and that the source text is reported to state it
No claim about calendars, seasons or astronomy beyond the arithmetic of the source text's own counts, and no claim that the year or the nodes describe any real sky
The near-miss analysis shows that the reported node is not closer than the grid forces; it does not show that no alignment between heads and seasons exists

No floating-point value enters any acceptance test: every assertion in checker.py compares integers or exact rationals, and the rounded decimal renderings the evidence carries for readability are not read back by any acceptance test of the checker
No native Rust witness, no claim promotion beyond bounded-external-experiment, no Seal, no library admission
residual: What is established is a set of exact statements about declared finite objects: that the four clauses transcribed into this contract from the source text's own statement of the head number generate exactly the coordinate formula of the earlier notes, so the address table is not merely an inference from a symbol range; that the nine heads the text's own nine-fold series names are a fiber over two of the four places and so are visible to the address, while the split at forty-seven is visible to no proper subset of the places and to no modulus below eighty-one; that a split the text itself pairs across, seven and eight against forty-seven and forty-eight, is carried by one displacement of order three, so the two boundaries are translates of each other; that the river diagram's pairing is the quotient by five, with a single fixed point that exists only because its partner falls outside the range; and that the reported calendar near miss is worse than the median node and behind a node more than seventy-six times closer, because the grid of head boundaries puts every node within nine quarters of a day of a boundary no matter what the data are. Nothing here decides any question about a text. In particular the four transcribed clauses are a transcription of a quotation and are not collated against any edition, so the check is that the transcription generates the coordinate formula and not that the text states it; the two invisibility results are about two declared algebras and not about cause; the translate relation is recorded and not explained; the calendar arithmetic is the source text's own and no claim is made that it describes a sky; and the near-miss result removes one piece of evidence without supplying any. The document quotes verbatim clauses of a classical text and identifies their source, and it opens no corpus.
